svg.text: 1 · TOPOLOGY: FROM THE ACCESS NETWORK TO THE SERVICES
PHYSICAL MACHINE ASUS ROG Strix G18 · HYPERVISOR HV01 (TeneT)
Fedora 44 · KVM/QEMU · libvirt · Cockpit · firewalld · SELinux enforcing · 30 GiB RAM · 952 GB NVMe, LUKS-encrypted · BTRFS + Snapper
libvirt NAT network “default” · bridge virbr0 · 192.168.122.0/24 · WAN side
Isolated bridge br-tenet · LAN 10.10.10.0/24 · no physical NIC · firewalld zone lab-tenet
All traffic to the outside goes through pfSense. The host relays nothing between its networks (F-13). Each Linux server has a host firewall (ufw), the DC its Domain profile.
Wazuh agents: 001 fedora · 002 Win-Server-DC · 003 lnx-dc01 → SIEM 1514/1515. Monitoring: fedora scrapes .10 (9182), .40 (9100), pfSense (SNMP 161).
Cross resolution: Windows DC → infrasec.internal via a conditional forwarder to .11; Samba → infrasec.local via pfSense (PV-08).
2 · THE SAME LAB, LAYER BY LAYER (OSI MODEL)
AD DS, LDAP, Kerberos, DNS, SMB 3, HTTPS (Cockpit,
Grafana, Zabbix, Wazuh), Wazuh agent protocol, SNMP
AGDLP and RBAC, GPO, 14/20-char passwords and lockout,
Wazuh rules 100100-100320, SMB audit, FIM whodata
TLS on web consoles and LDAPS (636), SMB
signing and encryption, JSON alert serialisation
SIEM certificate authority kept encrypted off
the SIEM (F-22); gpg AES-256 vault on the host
Kerberos tickets, SSH sessions, SMB sessions,
stateful pfSense, default deny; ufw on the SIEM and
Samba (F-15, F-25); Domain profile on the DC
tunnel 10.10.20.0/24; routing and NAT by pfSense
a single exit (pfSense); host forwarding blocked
by the lab-tenet zone (F-13); key-based WireGuard
Linux bridges br-tenet and virbr0, vnetN taps,
br-tenet without a physical NIC: isolated LAN;
br_netfilter not loaded (VM-to-VM traffic stays L2)
ASUS ROG Strix G18: 952 GB NVMe, 30 GiB RAM,
Wi-Fi wlo1; no cable to the lab LAN
